etymologies.etymologyHTML:
From Middle English encresen, borrowed from Anglo-Norman encreistre, from Latin increscere (“to increase”), from in (“in, on”) + crescō (“grow”).

The noun is from Middle English encres, from the verb.

definitions.definition: (intransitive) (of a quantity, etc.) To become larger or greater, to greaten.

quote.citation: 1611, The Holy Bible, […] (King James Version), London:  […]  Robert Barker, […], →OCLC, Genesis 7:17:
quote.text: The waters increased and bare up the ark.

quote.citation: c. 1603–1604 (date written), William Shakespeare, “The Tragedie of Othello, the Moore of Venice”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies […] (First Folio), London:  […]  Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, [Act II, scene i]:
quote.text: The heavens forbid / But that our loves and comforts should increase, / Even as our days do grow!

quote.citation: 1729, [Jonathan Swift], A Modest Proposal for Preventing the Children of Poor People from Being a Burthen to Their Parents, or the Country, and for Making Them Beneficial to the Publick, Dublin:  […]  S[arah] Harding, […], →OCLC, page 7:
quote.text: I have reckoned upon a Medium, that a Child juſt born vvill vveigh 12 pounds, and in a ſolar Year if tollerably nurſed encreaſeth to 28 Pound.

quote.citation: 1998, Dieter Schuocker, Handbook of the Eurolaser Academy, Springer Science & Business Media, →ISBN, page 51:
quote.text: This contribution reduces with increasing distance p from the emitting surface element dA, due to conservation of energy, as the wave energy distributed across the spherical wave front remains constant, while the radius increases during ...

quote.citation: 2019 February 3, “UN Study: China, US, Japan Lead World AI Development”, in Voice of America‎[1], archived from the original on 7 February 2019:
quote.text: The report said that deep learning methods increased from just 118 patent requests in 2013 to nearly 2,400 in 2016.

quote.citation: 2013 July-August, Fenella Saunders, “Tiny Lenses See the Big Picture”, in American Scientist:
quote.text: The single-imaging optic of the mammalian eye offers some distinct visual advantages. Such lenses can take in photons from a wide range of angles, increasing light sensitivity. They also have high spatial resolution, resolving incoming images in minute detail.

definitions.definition: To multiply by the production of young; to be fertile, fruitful, or prolific.

quote.citation: a. 1677 (date written), Matthew Hale, The Primitive Origination of Mankind, Considered and Examined According to the Light of Nature, London:  […]  William Godbid, for William Shrowsbery, […], published 1677, →OCLC:
quote.text: Fishes are infinitely more numerous of increasing than Beasts or Birds, as appears by the numerous Spawn.

definitions.definition: (astronomy, intransitive) To become more nearly full; to show more of the surface; to wax.
An amount by which a quantity is increased.

quote.citation: 2013 July-August, Philip J. Bushnell, “Solvents, Ethanol, Car Crashes & Tolerance”, in American Scientist:
quote.text: Surprisingly, this analysis revealed that acute exposure to solvent vapors at concentrations below those associated with long-term effects appears to increase the risk of a fatal automobile accident. Furthermore, this increase in risk is comparable to the risk of death from leukemia after long-term exposure to benzene, another solvent, which has the well-known property of causing this type of cancer.

quote.citation: 2018, VOA Learning English > China's Melting Glacier Brings Visitors, Adds to Climate Concerns‎[2]:
quote.text: She says an increase in melting from climate change may put that at risk.

definitions.definition: For a quantity, the act or process of becoming larger

quote.citation: 1599, [Thomas] Nashe, Nashes Lenten Stuffe, […], London:  […]  [Thomas Judson and Valentine Simmes] for N[icholas] L[ing] and C[uthbert] B[urby] […], →OCLC, page 2:
quote.text: That infortunate imperfit Embrion of my idle houres the Ile of Dogs before mentioned, breeding vnto me ſuch bitter throwes in the teaming as it did, and the tempeſtes that aroſe at his birth, ſo aſtoniſhing outragious and violent as if my braine had bene conceiued of another Hercules, I was ſo terrifyed with my owne encreaſe (like a woman long trauailing to bee deliuered of a monſter) that it was no ſooner borne but I was glad to run from it.

definitions.definition: (knitting) The creation of one or more new stitches; see Increase (knitting).
